[[[ To any NSA and FBI agents reading my email: please consider    ]]]
[[[ whether defending the US Constitution against all enemies,     ]]]
[[[ foreign or domestic, requires you to follow Snowden's example. ]]]

The problem that we have in Emacs is due to a confusion about the
meaning of the GNU Coding Standards' rules for referring to nonfree
programs.  The underlying correction calls for clarification of those.

We will also need to establish a new procedure for judging packages
for GNU ELPA and NonGNU ELPA.  As a first step, I ask people to be
careful that new packages added to ELPA do not run or communicate with
nonfree programs.  The ultimate rule will not be as strict as that,
but we can defer packages which do run or communicate with nonfree
programs until after the new procedure.

--

[[[ To any NSA and FBI agents reading my email: please consider    ]]]
[[[ whether defending the US Constitution against all enemies,     ]]]
[[[ foreign or domestic, requires you to follow Snowden's example. ]]]

  > It is okay to disagree. Let me just correct you that SaaSS is SaaSS no 
  > matter if it runs free software or non-free software. When user uses 
  > service as a software substitute, that is SaaSS.

That is correct.

To make it clear why, let's pick the clearest possible case: let's
suppose that the programs doing the work of the SaaSS site are all
GPL-covered.  If you ran them on your own machine, that would be fine
-- you would have control of them, there.  You would decide whether
to modify them; no one else could do that to you.

But you can't have control over how those GPL-covered programs run on
Mr Big's server, because those are his copies, not yours.  He can
modify them and not tell you, and you can't tell whether he did, nor
override his changes.

  > So what should GNU project do when there is no free alternative? The 
  > answer is not to use SaaSS and to work on the free replacement. The 
  > right answer is not to drive users to SaaSS in the meantime because the 
  > free alternative is hard. Making GNU was hard enough itself, yet we have 
  > it, so people can build free replacement hardware and software.

You've stated it well.  That philosophy is what keeps us aiming for
the overall goal of freedom; if we depart from it, we will be
sidetracked and cease to head for the goal.

But we don't need to keep discussing this on emacs-devel.

On Wed, 14 Oct 2026 at 00:25, Ami Fischman <ami@fischman.org> wrote:

> Quoting PROBLEMS: "This is a byproduct of GTK's not providing any means
> of probing for a display connection before committing to opening one, and cannot
> be addressed by Emacs."
> It seems to me that we could work around the lack of the above means by
> fork'ing and gtk_init'ing in the child (and then _exit(0)'ing), and using
> the exit status of the child as an indication of whether gtk_init is
> likely[*] to fail and so we should inhibit_window_system=1 in the parent.
>

There's a simpler solution: calling gtk_init_check, which does not call
exit. In fact, gtk_init essentially implemented like this:

void
gtk_init (int *argc, char ***argv)
  if (!gtk_init_check (argc, argv))
    {
      exit (1);
    }
}

Gtk_init_check has either been introduced in GTK after the PROBLEMS entry
was written, or the entry author did not research the problem.

Hey folks,

I'm not sure if anyone finds this useful or cares, but I've written a
remote agent for LSP, git, and file contents.  Ultimately I made it because
I had another project where remote access for these small short queries was
latency-heavy, especially with SSH jump boxes or teleport.

But hey, I had the same problems making remote dev via emacs, so why not
double up?

Scrutiny-agent (GPL)
https://github.com/five-rivers/scrutiny-agent/tree/main/emacs has some
emacs integration to speed up TRAMP, eglot, and magit where it can.

If you find it useful, great!  If not, well, I'd appreciate some feedback
or changes.  Hot-hacking this into a bunch of other folks' emacs packages
is a stack of shaky hacks so I'm eager for a more stable solution.
Especially if it's a way to make emacs faster for the key
software-development workflows.

I shamelessly used claude to do the grunt work here, so if y'all think
major changes are needed, I don't mind making claude doing a lot of work :-)

Cheers,
 - Lally Singh

Hi

my apologies upfront if this is out-of-scope, but with so much discussion
of LLM integration, I still miss an aspect I feel is at the foundation of
"The Discussion":

User C is a contributor
User M is a maintainer

C contributes a patch conforming to the guidelines and standards, i.e. FSF
paperwork done and no LLM involved.

M uses an ideal LLM that would be acceptable to keep track and inspect the
patch and possibly validate it.

There is doubt that feeding the LLM with the patch "trains" it, adding to
its "knowledge base".

If M then goes on and uses the LLM outside the scope of Emacs, what are the
implications?

Once again, sorry if this conjures up a new storm, but this has been
bugging me a lot lately.

Best, /PA

Pedro Andres Aranda Gutierrez <paaguti@gmail.com> writes:

> C contributes a patch conforming to the guidelines and standards, i.e. FS=
F paperwork done and no LLM involved.
=E2=80=A6
> If M then goes on and uses the LLM outside the scope of Emacs, what are t=
he implications?

If court decisions on software follow the ruling by the Munich court on
music=C2=B9, code created by this LLM that is sufficiently similar to the
contributed patch would be bound to the same license as the patch.

=C2=B9 https://www.gesetze-bayern.de/Content/Document/Y-300-Z-GRURRS-B-2025=
-N-30204

But most LLMs are trained on huge amounts of copyleft code already, so
the probability of generated code being bound to copyleft licenses
doesn=E2=80=99t increase significantly by adding one more patch.

Best wishes,
Arne

hei=C3=9Ft politisch sein,
ohne es zu merken.

On Wed, 14 Oct 2026 at 10:53, Pedro Andres Aranda Gutierrez
<paaguti@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> User C is a contributor
> User M is a maintainer
>
> C contributes a patch conforming to the guidelines and standards, i.e. FS=
F paperwork done and no LLM involved.
>
> M uses an ideal LLM that would be acceptable to keep track and inspect th=
e patch and possibly validate it.
>
> There is doubt that feeding the LLM with the patch "trains" it, adding to=
 its "knowledge base".

An ideal spherical LLM in a vacuum will not be trained this way.

Training an LLM involves vast amounts of computing power and time. On
the other hand, inferencing a pre-trained LLM takes much smaller
computing effort.

So, in practical use, an LLM is immutable. Any state that the user
wants persisted, is inside the session.

> If M then goes on and uses the LLM outside the scope of Emacs, what are t=
he implications?

In practical use, for a task outside the scope of Emacs, M will start
a separate session. And the LLM itself is immutable and stateless. So
there will be no information transfer from C=E2=80=99s patch into M=E2=80=
=99s separate
task.

Dear Yuri,

LLMs are immutable for as long that controller of the weights keep it 
immutable. There is no such general rule. Sole inference can retain LLM 
as immutable and yet not, depending on the model and various conditions.

See here https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B on the right side 
little below, you can see 193 adapters, 536 fine tunes...

If the LLM is remote — a SaaSS service — then the patch is sent to that 
service's server. What happens to it there is governed by the service's 
terms, not by the technical fact that inference does not update the 
weights.

The inference doesn't update the weights, but information user sends to 
server, especially if SaaSS, can be used to update the LLM, and is 
constantly used so. Providers may log responses, prompts, retain them 
over time, use them for future training, share them with third parties, 
you name it -- so that depends on terms of service and we can't even 
know what SaaSS companies do with data without respecting the terms of 
service.

The patch was contributed by C. C contributed it under the FSF's 
copyright assignment or license, on the understanding that it would be 
used for Emacs. If M sends it to a remote service — even for review — M 
has sent C's work to a third party without C's knowledge or consent.

That is a separate issue from training. It is a matter of what M is 
authorized to do with C's contribution.

> M will start a separate session. And the LLM itself is immutable and 
> stateless. So there will be no information transfer from C's patch into 
> M's separate task.

If inference is done locally, in most cases users will mostly not use 
information immediately to modify the model, yet, 536+ users from above 
examples they could have done so. That is why I said "mostly" will not 
use it.

Adaptations and fine tunes can be done on low performance hardware like 
RTX 3090 that cost $800.

If the LLM is local, there are no implications. The patch stays on M's 
machine. There is no transfer, no retention, no training, and no third 
party involved.

If the LLM is remote SaaSS, the implications are:

- The patch is sent to the provider's server.
- The provider may retain it, log it, and use it according to its terms.
- The provider's terms decide whether it is used for training, shared, 
or retained.
- C's contribution has been sent to a third party without C's consent.
- The fact that sole inference in many cases does not update the model 
does not change any of this.

Jean Louis

P.S. There are LLMs that are meant to be updated in real time, or almost 
real time:

- JIT LoRA (Just-in-Time LoRA): This system modifies a running language 
model's weights mid-conversation using LoRA adapters. It updates its 
weights after every response via background backpropagation, with 
training completing in about 70 seconds for a small model on consumer 
hardware 
https://huggingface.co/Ex0bit/jit-lora/blob/03ac9731e3018ef0bbdbe5ab467d9687e278c43a/paper.pdf#1

- Dark RL: Provides an OnlineLLM interface for interactive, online 
learning. It uses a single model instance for both training and 
inference concurrently, allowing the model to learn from user feedback 
in real-time by updating LoRA adapters 
https://pypi.org/project/dark-rl/#1

And there are several other examples, so we can safely assume that 
future models will tend to be updated by user's input almost in the real 
time.

Hello,

We are submitting Emacs Reader[0] for GNU ELPA. I am the author and
co-maintainer of the package alongside Tushar (aka tusharhero,
CC'ed). Emacs Reader is a general-purpose document reader inside of GNU
Emacs, it can work with PDF, EPUB, MOBI, FB2 and other formats. It has
been designed with memory and performance efficiency in mind. It is much
more resource friendly compared to other alternatives such as the
built-in DocView or pdf-tools[1].

To achieve this, we let a dynamic module written in C do heavylifting of
rendering the document. This dynamic module has a single dependency:
MuPDF (libmupdf) of version 1.26.0 or newer. This is much more efficient
because we can keep the large image data cached in C memory and not have
to be throttled by Emacs' GC. Emacs' image cache only keeps a single
(current) page, the rest are stored in C without incurring a performance
cost.

While the package has been in development since ~1.5 years, we wanted to
ensure that it is really stable before making it part of ELPA. We now
feel confident about this.

We are about to make a new release, and we'd like to incorporate any
suggestions that arise from the review into the release. So, as soon as
the review is finished, we would release 0.4.0 (this is the version that
should be published).

Furthermore, the next major version (0.5.0) is planned to be based on
the canvas image type . We already have a branch that is in progress
towards this. It will allow us to have text selection, highlighting,
annotations and other features that are expected in a document
reader. Consequently these features would only work on Emacs 32 and
above.

While the submission is for ELPA, I would also ask if Reader can be
considered for core, either replacing or being alongside DocView. In my
opinion, this can be considered because Reader has only one external
dependency that DocView also has: MuPDF. Other than that, Reader can do
almost everything DocView can more efficiently. The only discrepancy is
that while DocView can open DjVu files, Reader can't.  This is because
MuPDF doesn't natively support this format, so we cannot have it as of
now. I am coordinating with MuPDF developers to include DjVu in the near
future.

We have been taking care of copyright assignment since the beginning of
the project, making sure anyone who contributes (legally) significantly
has done the copyright assignment with FSF. The CONTRIBUTORS file
contains all information regarding this. We have everyone's copyright
assigned except one contributor=E2=80=99s (prom), who tried to do the assig=
nment
but due to their university association I think it didn't work out. We
are unsure how to go forward with this, but their (non-trivial) changes
are a bit above 15LOC, around 22 LOC of changes made to the
Makefile. Their code fixed a few issues when building Emacs Reader on MS
Windows[2].  We'd like your advice on what can be done here.

Lastly, we would greatly appreciate a thorough review and any feedback
on the package. The Emacs Lisp files are in the root directory, while
the C files live in render/ directory.

Thank you.

[0]: https://codeberg.org/monadicsheep/emacs-reader

Reader with the two. https://emacsconf.org/2025/talks/reader/
[2]: These commits:
https://codeberg.org/MonadicSheep/emacs-reader/commit/43b23e19e7a6e0c8ba07a=

Thanks Johan.
I also thought calling gtk_init_check during init_display_interactive would
be a simpler solution, but it turns out that it sets process-wide global
statics so that only the arguments passed to its first call have an effect
which requires a larger restructuring to pgtk_term_init to cope with
gtk-already-initialized.
Further, since -name / x-resource-name are only known once Lisp has run,
the program name has to be fixed later with g_set_prgname (and on X, GDK=E2=
=80=99s
leader window still gets the wrong name). It also opens the display before
early-init.el runs, so GDK/GTK env vars set there no longer affect the
first display.
Doing the probe in a forked child avoids all of this.

Cheers,
-Ami

Jo=E3o T=E1vora [2026-10-14 08:10:39] wrote:
>     Sending can yield to timers and process output, causing reentrant
>     calls to the request-making and reply-processing code.
>     For example, if the server takes its time to read a big request on
>     the other side of the pipe, the send blocks and a timer may make
>     another request.

This relates to a recurring problem we see for example when Edebugging
process filters: a first incoming packet causes entry into the Edebugged
filter function, and while we're steeping through that call to the
filter, another incoming packet may arrive causing Emacs to re-enter the
filter function even though we haven't yet finished running the
first call.

In the past I have suggested we should change the C code to disallow
that (i.e. to suspend reading process output from PROC while we're
running its process filter), but that would break some code.

I still think we should do that (presumably with some option to allow
using old code that needs the old behavior), but in the mean time, maybe
we should provide a `no-reentry` wrapper function, like:

    (defun no-reentry (f)
      (let ((busy nil)
            (pending nil))
        (lambda (proc string)
          (if busy (push string pending)
            (setq busy t)
            (unwind-protect
                (while string
                  (funcall f proc string)
                  (when pending
                    (setq string (mapconcat #'identity (nreverse pending)))
                    (setq pending nil)))
              (setq busy nil))))))

And yes, the same holds for timers, so this `no-rentry` could be
useful there as well, tho I'd also prefer if timers behaved like
that natively (i.e. repeating timers rearm themselves only after
the timer function finish running).


=3D=3D=3D Stefan

Content-Type: text/plain


> Also, can you confirm that all of your contributors didn't use LLMs to
> generate any of the code they submitted?
>
> Thanks for your diligence.

Yes. The project's description states in caps that we do not accept any LLM generated content. And every time there has been a PR, we ask them whether there was any LLM involved, and check the PR ourselves for any signs of LLM usage. If any of it suggests remotely the usage of a LLM, we close the PR. We try to remain as unntained from any LLM generated code as well, and always reimplement from scratch. An example of this can be seen here:

https://codeberg.org/MonadicSheep/emacs-reader/pulls/181

We never had to do the fix it like in the PR, I did a big refactor instead which indirectly fixed the bug.

Regards,

Divya Ranjan Pattanaik,
Philosophy, Mathematics, Libre Software.

https://codeberg.org/MonadicSheep/emacs-reader/pulls/181

We never had to do the fix like in the PR, I did a big refactor
instead which indirectly fixed the bug.

Divya Ranjan Pattanaik <divya@dialetheia.xyz> writes:

> Hello,
>
> We are submitting Emacs Reader[0] for GNU ELPA. I am the author and
> co-maintainer of the package alongside Tushar (aka tusharhero,
> CC'ed). Emacs Reader is a general-purpose document reader inside of GNU
> Emacs, it can work with PDF, EPUB, MOBI, FB2 and other formats. It has
> been designed with memory and performance efficiency in mind. It is much
> more resource friendly compared to other alternatives such as the
> built-in DocView or pdf-tools[1].
>
> To achieve this, we let a dynamic module written in C do heavylifting of
> rendering the document. This dynamic module has a single dependency:
> MuPDF (libmupdf) of version 1.26.0 or newer. This is much more efficient
> because we can keep the large image data cached in C memory and not have
> to be throttled by Emacs' GC. Emacs' image cache only keeps a single
> (current) page, the rest are stored in C without incurring a performance
> cost.
>
> While the package has been in development since ~1.5 years, we wanted to
> ensure that it is really stable before making it part of ELPA. We now
> feel confident about this.
>
> We are about to make a new release, and we'd like to incorporate any
> suggestions that arise from the review into the release. So, as soon as
> the review is finished, we would release 0.4.0 (this is the version that
> should be published).
>
> Furthermore, the next major version (0.5.0) is planned to be based on
> the canvas image type . We already have a branch that is in progress
> towards this. It will allow us to have text selection, highlighting,
> annotations and other features that are expected in a document
> reader. Consequently these features would only work on Emacs 32 and
> above.

I think this will be interesting, as it seems like it will be the first
larger project to seriously use the canvas image type.  I think we have
corresponded about this off-list, but I think it will be important to
ensure that we are not creating little islands of custom UI/UX within
the these images that lead to a fragmented and inconsnstent package
space.

> While the submission is for ELPA, I would also ask if Reader can be
> considered for core, either replacing or being alongside DocView.=20

My guestimate is that replacing it unlikely, since people might be
depending on doc-view and have local customisations that assume it is
already built-in.  My advice would be to stick to ELPA for now, until
the package can mature with more users (not just time)

>                                                                   In my
> opinion, this can be considered because Reader has only one external
> dependency that DocView also has: MuPDF.=20

DocView has other fall-backs (prominently Ghostscript), and only
requires a MuPDF executable to be installed for certain file types like
Epub.

>                                          Other than that, Reader can do
> almost everything DocView can more efficiently. The only discrepancy is
> that while DocView can open DjVu files, Reader can't.  This is because
> MuPDF doesn't natively support this format, so we cannot have it as of
> now. I am coordinating with MuPDF developers to include DjVu in the near
> future.

That is nice to hear!

> We have been taking care of copyright assignment since the beginning of
> the project, making sure anyone who contributes (legally) significantly
> has done the copyright assignment with FSF. The CONTRIBUTORS file
> contains all information regarding this. We have everyone's copyright
> assigned except one contributor=E2=80=99s (prom), who tried to do the ass=
ignment
> but due to their university association I think it didn't work out. We
> are unsure how to go forward with this, but their (non-trivial) changes
> are a bit above 15LOC, around 22 LOC of changes made to the
> Makefile. Their code fixed a few issues when building Emacs Reader on MS
> Windows[2].  We'd like your advice on what can be done here.

This is something for Eli and/or Sean to comment on.  CC'ed.

> Lastly, we would greatly appreciate a thorough review and any feedback
> on the package. The Emacs Lisp files are in the root directory, while
> the C files live in render/ directory.

Looking at just the Elisp code, most of it seems to be either
arithmetical+state maintainance business logic or just fine Lisp.  FWIW
I have a few comments and suggestions here, but sadly not much more than
this:

Hi all,

For the past two months or so I've been slowly working on pulling
Eglot's code actions machinery out into a new library,
lisp/progmodes/refactor.el, so that it's not tied to LSP anymore.  The
attached patch is the result of that work.

It's a :core package that's setup as an Eglot dependency, just like
Flymake, ElDoc, Xref and others.

This fell partially out of an old request from Eli to work on something
like this (or so I seem to remember) and, more recently, from some
discussion with Eshel Yaron about Flymake having "quickfix" commands,
where he and I disagreed on how to implement it.  Quickfixes are
supported of course, and they're just another kind of action.

The working concept of actions came from LSP, obviously.  I and probably
most Eglot users have been using them for many years now.  It's very
useful, I use rename hundreds of times a day, and other actions also
quite frequently.  So IMO it's a battle-tested architecture to adopt in
refactor.el.

Roughly, refactor.el has:

- No manual yet, but the Commentary section is decently fleshed out and
  could be the start of a manual.

- Some Elisp entry points for backend authors:
  refactor-backend-functions, a hook much like xref-backend-functions,
  except every backend contributes.  Backends implement a few generics:
  refactor-backend-actions, refactor-backend-execute,
  refactor-backend-rename-bounds and refactor-backend-rename.

- Commands: M-x refactor, refactor-rename, refactor-quickfix,
  refactor-fix-all, refactor-extract, refactor-inline, refactor-rewrite
  and refactor-organize-imports.

- A small hierarchy of action kinds (quickfix, rewrite, extract...),
  extensible with refactor-defkind.

- Changesets: lists of operations (file edits, creations, renames,
  deletions) that refactor-apply-changeset carries out, honoring
  refactor-confirmation (summary, diff, etc.).  That's what used to be
  eglot-confirm-server-edits.

- refactor-suggestion-mode: the ElDoc-based "actions available here"
  indicator Eglot had.

Eglot is now just one backend, and its old commands and variables are
obsolete aliases that point to the new commands.  I've been daily
driving this in Eglot for some weeks now.  The only visible backward
incompatibility I've noticed is that the keybinding I had for
eglot-code-actions doesn't show up in the ElDoc suggestion anymore, so
instead of my clangd saying '[f4]: Swap operands to =3D=3D' it now says 'M-x
refactor: Swap operands to =3D=3D'.  That's just because I haven't bothered
to bind f4 to M-x refactor.  The binding itself still works fine.

The point of all this is, of course, to enable _other_ consumers of
the API.  So I'm also attaching elisp-refactor.el, a small Emacs Lisp
backend.  To be very clear, it's a ~200-line toy, and it's 99% vibe
coded (gasp!), so it probably can't be merged, but it's somewhat
usable and illustrates the different aspects of the API:

- Rename: refactor-rename renames a symbol within the current defun,
  very very dumbly: it's a textual replace, so it happily hits
  strings, comments and unrelated same-named things.

- Actions that are only suggested in some places in the buffer, for
  example "Convert `if' to `cond'" when point is on an `if' -- a very
  modestly useful refactoring, I know.  Another action is "Expand
  macro once/fully" with point on a macro call -- this one is useful
  and defines its own `macroexpand' "action kind", just to show that
  off.

- Quickfixes for Flymake diagnostics: I used the "Unused lexical
  variable" warnings that Flymake already reports in Elisp buffers as
  an example.  Now they have a quickfix that adds the underscore, and
  M-x refactor-fix-all does it for the whole buffer.

To try it, with the patch applied:

  (load "/path/to/elisp-refactor.el")
  (add-hook 'emacs-lisp-mode-hook #'elisp-refactor-mode)

I did try to make a smarter version of the toy, but the point for now is
not to do the Lisp language heavy lifting.  Maybe if someone (tm) works
on this, Emacs 32 will have nice Elisp refactoring with renaming,
function extractions, numerous types of quickfixes, etc.

I have been a private version of this for the SLY Common Lisp IDE
which uses much more accurate code-walking techniques.  It uses a
source-tracking reader and "mnesic" macroexpansion, two techniques
described in my ELS 2020 paper (https://zenodo.org/records/3742759).
Let me know if you're into the details.

Comments welcome, of course,
Jo=C3=A3o

Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 19:31:53 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] Add refactor.el; move generic code actions machinery out of
 Eglot

Most of Eglot's code actions code wasn't LSP-specific, and could be
useful to other major and minor modes.  Extract it to new refactor.el,
leaving Eglot with just the LSP-specific backend; old entry points now
redirect there via obsolete aliases.

* lisp/progmodes/refactor.el: New file.

* lisp/progmodes/eglot.el (refactor-backend-name, refactor-backend-actions)
(refactor-backend-execute, refactor-backend-rename)
(refactor-backend-rename-bounds): New cl-defmethods.
(eglot-refactor-backend, eglot--translate-workspace-edit): New helpers.
(eglot--refactor-kinds): New variable.
(eglot--managed-mode): Register refactor backend, start
refactor-suggestion-mode.
(eglot--apply-workspace-edit, eglot--apply-text-edits): Rework to use
refactor.el.
(eglot--flymake-diag-type): Use refactor diagnostic types.
(eglot-mode-line-format): Drop eglot-mode-line-action-suggestion.
(eglot-code-action-suggestion, eglot--read-execute-code-action)
(eglot--code-action-bounds, eglot--rename-interactive)
(eglot--confirm-server-edits, eglot--propose-changes-as-diff): Delete.
(eglot--code-action): Delete macro.
(eglot--suggestion-overlay, eglot--fringe-action): Delete.
(eglot-code-actions, eglot-rename, eglot-code-actions-at-mouse)
(eglot-code-action-organize-imports, eglot-code-action-extract)
(eglot-code-action-inline, eglot-code-action-rewrite)
(eglot-code-action-quickfix): Add obsolete aliases.
(eglot-code-action-indications, eglot-code-action-indicator)
(eglot-diagnostics-map, eglot-confirm-server-edits): Add obsolete
variable aliases.
(eglot-code-action-indicator-face): Add obsolete face alias.
(eglot-mode-line-action-suggestion): Make obsolete.

* test/lisp/progmodes/eglot-tests.el (eglot-test-rename-a-symbol): Tweak.

+(cl-defun eglot--translate-workspace-edit (wedit)
+  "Compute list of `refactor-operation' from LSP workspace edit WEDIT."
+  (let ((pathify (symbol-function 'eglot-uri-to-path))
+        (text-edit-op
+         (lambda (path edits version)
+           (make-instance
+            'refactor-file-edit
+            :file path
+            :edits
+            (lambda ()
+              (eglot--apply-text-edits edits version t))))))
+    (eglot--dbind ((WorkspaceEdit) changes documentChanges) wedit
+      (append
+       (mapcar
+        (lambda (ch)
+          (pcase (plist-get ch :kind)
+            ("create"
+             (eglot--dbind ((CreateFile) uri ((:options o))) ch
+               (make-instance
+                'refactor-file-creation
+                :file (funcall pathify uri)
+                :if-exists (cond ((plist-get o :ignoreIfExists) 'skip)
+                                 ((plist-get o :overwrite) 'overwrite)
+                                 (t 'error)))))
+            ("rename"
+             (eglot--dbind ((RenameFile) oldUri newUri ((:options o))) ch
+               (make-instance
+                'refactor-file-renaming
+                :from (funcall pathify oldUri)
+                :to (funcall pathify newUri)
+                :if-exists (cond ((plist-get o :ignoreIfExists) 'skip)
+                                 ((plist-get o :overwrite) 'overwrite)
+                                 (t 'error)))))
+            ("delete"
+             (eglot--dbind ((DeleteFile) uri ((:options o))) ch
+               (make-instance
+                'refactor-file-deletion
+                :file (funcall pathify uri)
+                :recursive (plist-get o :recursive)
+                :if-missing (if (plist-get o :ignoreIfNotExists)
+                                'skip 'error))))
+            (_
+             ;; It's a TextDocumentEdit (no kind field)
+             (eglot--dbind ((TextDocumentEdit) textDocument edits) ch
+               (eglot--dbind ((VersionedTextDocumentIdentifier) uri versio=
n)
+                   textDocument
+                 (funcall text-edit-op (funcall pathify uri)
+                          edits version))))))
+        documentChanges)
+       (unless (and changes documentChanges)
+         ;; Prefer `documentChanges' over sort-of-deprecated `changes'.
+         (cl-loop for (uri edits) on changes by #'cddr
+                  collect (funcall text-edit-op (funcall pathify uri)
+                                   edits nil)))))))

+            (eglot--code-action-params :beg beg :end end :only lsp-rkind
+                                       :triggerKind trigger-kind)))
+      (cond
+       (callback
+        (eglot--async-request
+         server
+         :textDocument/codeAction
+         params
+         :success-fn (lambda (actions) (funcall callback (convert actions)=
))
+         :hint :textDocument/codeAction)
+        :async)
+       (t
+        (convert (eglot--request server :textDocument/codeAction params)))=
))))
+
+(cl-defmethod refactor-backend-execute
+    ((_backend (eql eglot)) action)
+  (eglot-execute (eglot--current-server-or-lose) (oref action data)))
+
+(cl-defmethod refactor-backend-rename-bounds
+  ((_backend (eql eglot)))
+  (let* ((rename-support (eglot-server-capable-or-lose :renameProvider))
+         (prepare-support (and (listp rename-support)
+                               (plist-get rename-support :prepareProvider)=
)))
+    (cond (prepare-support
+           (let ((x (eglot--request (eglot--current-server-or-lose)
+                                    :textDocument/prepareRename
+                                    (eglot--TextDocumentPositionParams))))
+             (cond ((null x) nil)
+                   ((plist-get x :range) (eglot-range-region (plist-get x =
:range)))
+                   ((plist-get x :defaultBehavior) (bounds-of-thing-at-poi=
nt 'symbol))
+                   (t (eglot-range-region x)))))
+          (t (bounds-of-thing-at-point 'symbol)))))
+
+(cl-defmethod refactor-backend-rename ((_backend (eql eglot)) newname)
+  (let ((server (eglot--current-server-or-lose)))
+    (eglot--translate-workspace-edit
+     (eglot--request server :textDocument/rename
+                     `(,@(eglot--TextDocumentPositionParams)
+                       :newName ,newname)))))
+
+(define-obsolete-function-alias 'eglot-code-actions 'refactor "32.1")
+(define-obsolete-function-alias 'eglot-rename 'refactor-rename "32.1")

+  'refactor-organize-imports "32.1")

+  'refactor-extract "32.1")

+  'refactor-rewrite "32.1")

+;;; refactor.el --- Language-agnostic refactoring interface  -*- lexical-b=
inding: t; -*-
+
+;; Copyright (C) 2026 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
+;; Author: Jo=C3=A3o T=C3=A1vora <joaotavora@gmail.com>
+
+;; Version: 0.1
+;; Keywords: convenience, languages
+;; Package-Requires: ((emacs "28.1"))
+
+;; This is a GNU ELPA :core package.  Avoid adding functionality that
+;; is not available in the version of Emacs recorded above.
+
+;; This file is part of GNU Emacs.
+
+;; GNU Emacs is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify
+;; it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by
+;; the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or
+;; (at your option) any later version.
+
+;; GNU Emacs is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
+;; but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
+;; MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.  See the
+;; GNU General Public License for more details.
+
+;; You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
+;; along with GNU Emacs.  If not, see <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
+
+;;; Commentary:
+
+;; `refactor.el' is a library for adding refactoring support for any
+;; programming language.  A refactoring, or refactor, is any rewrite to
+;; a program that maintains its intended meaning, while (hopefully)
+;; improving it.  It could be extracting a function, inlining a
+;; variable, renaming an identifier, organizing imports, or
+;; automatically fixing a diagnostic.  In `refactor.el' each such
+;; potential rewrite is called an _action_ and embodied by the
+;; `refactor-action' object.
+;;
+;; Note that this library is completely agnostic about the programming
+;; language and major mode.  By itself, it has no knowledge of how these
+;; actions are discovered and eventually carried out: that's for other
+;; Elisp programs to define and set up, in the form of `refactor.el'
+;; _backends_.  A very significant part of the code was extracted from
+;; Emacs' LSP client Eglot, which now contains a simpler backend that
+;; makes use of refactor.el.
+;;
+;;;; User interface
+;;
+;; In buffers where a working backend is set up, the library provides
+;; some useful UI: a number of interactive commands for selecting
+;; actions -- `refactor', `refactor-rename' and a few more shortcut
+;; commands -- as well as the `refactor-suggestion-mode' minor mode,
+;; which leverages the ElDoc system and endeavors to constantly keep the
+;; user informed of which actions are available.  This minor mode is the
+;; familiar "lightning bolt/lightbulb on the side" that some IDEs
+;; display.  The variable `refactor-indications' is its main point of
+;; customization.
+;;
+;; Each action has a "kind", which is used by the aforementioned
+;; shortcut commands.  For example, `refactor-quickfix' restricts
+;; actions at point to the specific kind `quickfix' and ignores are
+;; actions of other kids (like, say `extract' or `inline').  Depending
+;; on the number of actions avaiable and the specific command, actions
+;; are either automatically selected or presented to the user for
+;; selection.
+;;
+;; Once an action is selected, it is executed, but its changes aren't
+;; necessarily applied right away.  The variable `refactor-confirmation'
+;; controls whether and how the user confirms them first: as a summary
+;; in the minibuffer, as a diff of the proposed changes, or not at all.
+;; The choice can depend on the command, on the kinds of file
+;; operations involved, and on whether the affected files are visited
+;; in buffers.
+;;
+;;;; Elisp API
+;;
+;; The Elisp-facing parts of this library are useful for backend
+;; authors: there are two distinct Elisp-facing interfaces, independent
+;; of each other.  Either is useful alone, though they can and normally
+;; work together.
+;;
+;; - Action discovery and selection
+;;
+;;   The interactive commands are entry points that communicate with
+;;   "refactor backends", i.e. any object returned by
+;;   `refactor-backend-functions'.  The base `refactor' command asks
+;;   backends via `refactor-backend-actions' what "actions"
+;;   (i.e. potential refactorings) can be carried out for the buffer
+;;   near point.  This is much like `xref-backend-functions' except that
+;;   unlike Xref, every applicable backend contributes.  The backend who
+;;   provided the chosen action (regardless of how it was chosen) is
+;;   asked again to carry it out.  This invokes its implementation of
+;;   the `refactor-backend-execute' method.  Executing an action could
+;;   entail changes to the current buffer or to other buffers, even
+;;   changes to unvisited files, creation or deletion of files: the
+;;   library puts no constraints on the scope of an action.
+;;
+;; - Changeset application:
+;;
+;;   To simplify and give consistency to the execution of actions,
+;;   we use the concept of _changeset_, an ordered list of
+;;   `refactor-operation' objects.  Though not required, a normal
+;;   implementation of `refactor-backend-execute' would compute such a
+;;   changeset, then offer to apply it by calling
+;;   `refactor-apply-changeset'.  `refactor-apply-changeset' carries out
+;;   each `refactor-operation' -- edits to files, creation of files,
+;;   renaming and deletion of files -- according to certain rules.  For
+;;   example, it may offer a preview to the user as a summarized
+;;   description and ask for confirmation in the minibuffer, or it may
+;;   present the changeset as a diff, or it may skip confirmation
+;;   altogether.  This is according to the user preferences in
+;;   `refactor-confirmation'.  Note that an Elisp program may call this
+;;   directly for applying changes in a consistent and uniform manner
+;;   outside the context of `refactor-backend-execute'.
+;;
+;;; Code:
+
+(require 'cl-lib)
+(require 'eieio)
+(require 'flymake)
+
+(defgroup refactor nil
+  "Refactoring support." ; hmmm, a bit short no?
+  :prefix "refactor-"
+  :group 'tools)
+
+;;;; Backends
+;; JT@2026-08-21: While a hook may be overkill (a plain buffer-local
+;; variable would likely do), it matches the Xref precedent.
+
+(defvar refactor-backend-functions nil
+  "Special hook to find the refactor backends for the current context.
+Each function in this hook is called in turn with no arguments, and
+should return nil if it is not applicable, or a refactor backend, that
+is, a value on which the `refactor-backend-*' generic functions
+dispatch.  Unlike `xref-backend-functions' (which inspired this) every
+backend contributes: for example the actions each supplies are merged
+into a single list for the user to choose from.")
+
+(defun refactor-find-backends ()
+  "Return the refactor backends applicable in the current context.
+Run every function on `refactor-backend-functions' in turn and
+collect the non-nil backends they return."
+  (let (retval)
+    (run-hook-wrapped 'refactor-backend-functions
+                      (lambda (a)
+                        (when-let* ((x (funcall a))) (push x retval))
+                        nil))
+    (reverse retval)))
+
+(cl-defgeneric refactor-backend-name (backend)
+  "Return a short human-readable name for BACKEND."
+  (:method (backend) (symbol-name backend)))
+
+(cl-defgeneric refactor-backend-actions
+    (backend beg end &key rkind callback trigger-kind)
+  "Compute refactoring actions BACKEND offers between BEG and END.
+
+RKIND, if non-nil, restricts the result to that kind and its
+sub-kinds.
+
+If CALLBACK is nil, return the list of `refactor-action' objects
+directly; blocking to do so is acceptable.
+
+If CALLBACK is non-nil, either return the list of actions directly
+anyway (when that is cheap) or return `:async' after arranging for
+CALLBACK to be called with the list of actions eventually (but at most
+once).  CALLBACK may also be invoked synchronously, before this
+function returns.")
+
+(cl-defgeneric refactor-backend-execute (backend action)
+  "Have BACKEND carry ACTION out, by whatever means it likes."
+  (:method (_backend _action)
+   (error "Refactor backend doesn't know how to execute actions")))
+
+(cl-defgeneric refactor-backend-rename-bounds (backend)
+  "Return bounds of thing BACKEND could rename near point.
+If the return value is a cons of buffer positions (BEG . END), these are
+the bounds of the nearby thing that BACKEND claims as renameable.
+A nil return means BACKEND does not claim this as renameable."
+  (:method (_backend) nil))
+
+(cl-defgeneric refactor-backend-rename (backend newname)
+  "Compute a changeset renaming the identifier at point to NEWNAME."
+  (:method (_backend _newname) nil))

+;;;; Utils

+(defmacro refactor--defclass (name superclasses docstring &rest specs)
+  "Util for cutting down on defclass boilerplate.
+NAME, SUPERCLASSES and DOCSTRING are as in `defclass'.  Each of SPECS
+is (SLOT INITFORM SLOT-DOCSTRING)."
+  (declare (indent 2) (debug (&define name sexp stringp &rest sexp)))
+  `(defclass ,name ,superclasses
+     ,(mapcar (lambda (spec)
+                (cl-destructuring-bind (slot initform slotdoc) spec
+                  `(,slot :initarg ,(intern (concat ":" (symbol-name slot)=
))
+                          :initform ,initform
+                          :documentation ,slotdoc)))
+              specs)
+     :documentation ,docstring))
+
+
+;;;; Actions
+
+(refactor--defclass refactor-action ()
+  "A refactoring a backend offers to perform."
+  (title nil "One-line description, shown to the user.")
+  (kind nil "A symbol from `refactor-kinds', or nil.")
+  (preferred nil "Non-nil if this is the obvious choice here.")
+  (backend nil "The backend that offered this action.")
+  (data nil "Opaque payload, meaningful to the backend."))
+
+
+;;;; Kinds
+
+;; Every action is tagged with a "kind" symbol.  Could be e.g.
+;; `quickfix' or `extract'.  Kinds are organized in a hierarchy which is
+;; what RKIND in `refactor' matches against.  Specialized commands scope
+;; down to just some kinds: so `M-x refactor-quickfix' offers only
+;; actions tagged `quickfix'.  In contrast, asking for the `refactor'
+;; kind (with a prefix argument to `M-x refactor') also offers
+;; `extract', `inline', `rewrite' and `move' ones.  Plain `M-x refactor'
+;; doesn't filter, and offers everything.  Backends tag their actions
+;; with any of the kinds defined below or may use the macros to define
+;; their own.
+
+(defvar refactor-kinds nil
+  "List of all refactoring kinds defined so far, in definition order.")
+
+(defmacro refactor-defkind (name parent docstring)
+  "Define NAME as a kind of refactoring.
+PARENT is the kind NAME specializes, or nil if NAME is itself a
+top-level kind.  DOCSTRING describes NAME to the user."
+  (declare (doc-string 3) (indent 2))
+  `(progn
+     (put ',name 'refactor-kind-parent ',parent)
+     (put ',name 'refactor-kind-documentation ,docstring)
+     (unless (memq ',name refactor-kinds)
+       (setq refactor-kinds (append refactor-kinds (list ',name))))
+     ',name))
+
+(defun refactor-kind-matches-p (kind filter)
+  "Return non-nil if KIND is FILTER or one of its sub-kinds.
+A nil FILTER matches everything."
+  (or (null filter)
+      (cl-loop for k =3D kind then (get k 'refactor-kind-parent)
+               while k thereis (eq k filter))))
+
+(refactor-defkind quickfix nil "Fix a problem reported at point.")
+(refactor-defkind refactor nil "Change code without changing what it does.=
")
+(refactor-defkind extract refactor "Extract code into a new named entity.")
+(refactor-defkind inline refactor "Inline a named entity into its call sit=
es.")
+(refactor-defkind rewrite refactor "Restate code in a different form.")
+(refactor-defkind move refactor "Move an entity somewhere else.")
+(refactor-defkind source nil "Act on a file rather than on a selection.")
+(refactor-defkind organize-imports source "Tidy up import declarations.")
+(refactor-defkind fix-all source "Apply every fix available in the file.")
+
+
+;;;; Changesets
+
+;; A changeset is an ordered list of operations, each an instance of a
+;; class below.  Backends make them with `make-instance', and may
+;; subclass the classes for operations we haven't thought of;
+;; `refactor-apply-changeset' shows them to the user and carries them
+;; out.  FIXME: move this to the manual later.
+
+(refactor--defclass refactor-operation ()
+  "Superclass of the operations making up a changeset.")
+
+(refactor--defclass refactor-file-edit (refactor-operation)
+  "Operation changing the text of a single file."
+  (file nil "Absolute name of the file to change.")
+  (edits nil "\
+Either a list of (BEG END NEWTEXT), where BEG and END are integer
+positions valid in the widened buffer visiting the file, or a
+function of no arguments returning such a list, called with that
+buffer current.  Edits must not overlap."))
+
+(refactor--defclass refactor-file-creation (refactor-operation)
+  "Operation creating a file."
+  (file nil "Absolute name of the file to create.")
+  (contents nil "Initial contents, or nil for an empty file.")
+  (if-exists 'error "What to do if file exists: `error', `skip' or `overwr=
ite'."))
+
+(refactor--defclass refactor-file-renaming (refactor-operation)
+  "Operation renaming a file."
+  (from nil "Absolute name of the file to rename.")
+  (to nil "Absolute name to rename it to.")
+  (if-exists 'error "What to do if new name is taken: `error', `skip' or `=
overwrite'."))
+
+(refactor--defclass refactor-file-deletion (refactor-operation)
+  "Operation deleting a file."
+  (file nil "Absolute name of the file to delete.")
+  (recursive nil "Non-nil to delete a directory's contents too.")
+  (if-missing 'error "What to do if file does not exist: `error' or `skip'=
."))
+
+(cl-defgeneric refactor-operation-kind (operation)
+  "Return a symbol classifying OPERATION.
+One of `edit', `create', `rename' or `delete' (the symbols
+`refactor-confirmation' matches against)."
+  (:method ((_ refactor-file-edit)) 'edit)
+  (:method ((_ refactor-file-creation)) 'create)
+  (:method ((_ refactor-file-renaming)) 'rename)
+  (:method ((_ refactor-file-deletion)) 'delete))
+
+(cl-defgeneric refactor-describe (operation)
+  "Return a one-line description of OPERATION."
+  (:method ((op refactor-file-edit))
+   (with-slots (file edits) op
+     (if (functionp edits)
+         (format "Change `%s'" file)
+       (format "Change `%s' (%d change%s)" file
+               (length edits) (if (cdr edits) "s" "")))))
+  (:method ((op refactor-file-creation))
+   (format "Create `%s'" (oref op file)))
+  (:method ((op refactor-file-renaming))
+   (with-slots (from to) op
+     (format "Rename `%s' to `%s'" from to)))
+  (:method ((op refactor-file-deletion))
+   (format "Delete `%s'" (oref op file))))
+
+
+;;;; Collecting actions
+
+(cl-defun refactor--collect
+    (beg end &key rkind callback trigger-kind)
+  "Gather actions for BEG END from every applicable backend.
+
+This is the workhorse for `refactor' and `refactor-suggestion', the sync
+and async modes of collecting actions, respectively.
+
+If CALLBACK is nil, return the merged list of `refactor-action's.
+
+If CALLBACK is non-nil, return `:async' and call CALLBACK once with the
+merged list when every backend has delivered (which may happen before
+this function returns, depending on the backends).  A backend that
+signals an error counts as having delivered no actions."
+  (let ((slots
+         ;; Each slot is (BACKEND DELIVERED-P . ACTIONS), DELIVERED-P
+         ;; being non-nil once BACKEND has delivered ACTIONS, via its
+         ;; callback or by returning them.
+         (mapcar (lambda (backend) (list backend nil))
+                 (refactor-find-backends))))
+    (cl-labels
+        ((merged ()
+           ;; Keep the first of each title, in hook order rather than
+           ;; delivery order, so that earlier backends win clashes even
+           ;; if they are slower.
+           (cl-remove-duplicates (apply #'append (mapcar #'cddr slots))
+                                 :key (lambda (a) (oref a title))
+                                 :test #'equal :from-end t))
+         (deliver (result slot)
+           (setcar (cdr slot) t)
+           (setcdr (cdr slot) result)
+           (when (and callback (cl-every #'cadr slots))
+             (funcall callback (merged))))
+         (filter (actions)
+           (cl-remove-if-not
+            (lambda (a)
+              (refactor-kind-matches-p (oref a kind) rkind))
+            actions)))
+      (dolist (slot slots)
+        (condition-case-unless-debug oops
+            (let ((result
+                   (refactor-backend-actions
+                    (car slot) beg end
+                    :callback
+                    (and callback
+                         (lambda (result)
+                           (deliver (filter result) slot)))
+                    :rkind rkind
+                    :trigger-kind trigger-kind)))
+              ;; A backend may even call its callback before returning
+              ;; actual actions.  When it does, trust the callback's
+              ;; result over the return value.
+              (unless (or (cadr slot)
+                          (eq result :async))
+                (deliver (filter result) slot)))
+          (error
+           (message "refactor: backend %S failed: %S"
+                    (car slot) (cdr oops))
+           ;; Deliver no actions, unless already delivered.
+           (unless (cadr slot) (deliver nil slot)))))
+      (if callback :async (merged)))))
+
+
+;;;; Commands
+
+(defvar refactor--suggestion-overlay)
+
+(defun refactor--bounds ()
+  "Return (BEG END) for the current refactoring context.
+This is the active region, if any, else it's the span covering any
+Flymake diagnostics at point, else the bounds of the expression at
+point, else point."
+  (let (diags boftap)
+    (cond ((use-region-p) `(,(region-beginning) ,(region-end)))
+          ((setq diags (flymake-diagnostics (point) (point)))
+           (cl-loop for d in diags
+                    minimizing (flymake-diagnostic-beg d) into beg
+                    maximizing (flymake-diagnostic-end d) into end
+                    finally (cl-return (list beg end))))
+          ((setq boftap (bounds-of-thing-at-point 'sexp))
+           (list (car boftap) (cdr boftap)))
+          (t
+           (list (point) (point))))))
+
+(defun refactor--read-execute-action (actions)
+  "Choose and execute one of ACTIONS, a list of `refactor-action's.
+If there is only one, execute it without asking."
+  (let* ((menu-items (cl-loop for a in actions
+                              collect (cons (oref a title) a)))
+         (preferred-action
+          (cl-find-if (lambda (menu-item)
+                        (oref (cdr menu-item) preferred))
+                      menu-items))
+         (default-action (car (or preferred-action (car menu-items))))
+         (chosen (if (null (cdr menu-items))
+                     (cdr (car menu-items))
+                   (if (listp last-nonmenu-event)
+                       (x-popup-menu last-nonmenu-event
+                                     `("Refactor:"
+                                       ("dummy" ,@menu-items)))
+                     (cdr (assoc (completing-read
+                                  (format "Pick a refactoring (default %s)=
: "
+                                          default-action)
+                                  menu-items nil t nil nil default-action)
+                                 menu-items))))))
+    (when chosen (refactor-backend-execute (oref chosen backend) chosen))))
+
+;;;###autoload
+(defun refactor (beg &optional end rkind interactive)
+  "Find refactoring actions between BEG and END, and offer to run them.
+
+If RKIND, a symbol, is non-nil, restrict search to actions of that kind
+and its sub-kinds; interactively with a prefix arg, choose from
+`refactor-kinds'.
+
+Interactively, BEG and END default to automatically calculated bounds
+and a prefix argument prompts for KIND.
+
+When INTERACTIVE is nil, return the list of `refactor-action' objects."
+  (interactive
+   `(,@(refactor--bounds)
+     ,(and current-prefix-arg
+           (intern
+            (completing-read
+             "Kind of refactoring: "
+             (mapcar (lambda (kind)
+                       (cons (symbol-name kind) kind))
+                     refactor-kinds)
+             nil t)))
+     t))
+  (let* ((shortcut
+          ;; Check if we can do an optimization/shortcut.
+          ;; `refactor-suggestion' may just recently have computed
+          ;; exactly what we wanted, stashing it in
+          ;; `refactor--suggestion-overlay'.  Not when asked for a
+          ;; specific RKIND, though: those suggestions were requested
+          ;; with an "automatic" trigger kind, and backends may hold
+          ;; back some actions, like `fix-all' ones, in that case.
+          (and interactive
+               (null rkind)
+               (not (listp last-nonmenu-event)) ; not run by mouse
+               (overlay-buffer refactor--suggestion-overlay)
+               (=3D beg (overlay-start refactor--suggestion-overlay))
+               (=3D end (overlay-end refactor--suggestion-overlay))))
+         (actions
+          (if shortcut
+              ;; ...in which case we can skip re-contacting the backend.
+              (overlay-get refactor--suggestion-overlay 'refactor--actions)
+            (refactor--collect beg end :rkind rkind))))
+    (unless actions
+      (user-error (if rkind "No \"%s\" refactorings here" "No refactorings=
 here")
+                  rkind))
+    (if interactive (refactor--read-execute-action actions) actions)))
+
+(defmacro refactor--define-kind-command (name kind)
+  "Define NAME to execute KIND refactorings between BEG and END."
+  `(defun ,name (beg &optional end)
+     ,(format "Execute `%s' refactorings between BEG and END." kind)
+     (interactive (refactor--bounds))
+     (refactor beg end ',kind t)))
+
+(defun refactor--mouse-call (what &optional update-mode-line)
+  "Make an interactive lambda for calling WHAT with the mouse."
+  (lambda (event)
+    (interactive "e")
+    (let ((start (event-start event)))
+      (with-selected-window (posn-window start)
+        (save-excursion
+          (unless (posn-area start)
+            (goto-char (posn-point start)))
+          (call-interactively what)
+          (when update-mode-line
+            (force-mode-line-update t)))))))
+
+(defalias 'refactor-at-mouse (refactor--mouse-call 'refactor)
+  "Like `refactor', but intended for mouse events.")
+
+(refactor--define-kind-command refactor-organize-imports organize-imports)
+(refactor--define-kind-command refactor-extract extract)
+(refactor--define-kind-command refactor-inline inline)
+(refactor--define-kind-command refactor-rewrite rewrite)
+(refactor--define-kind-command refactor-quickfix quickfix)
+(refactor--define-kind-command refactor-fix-all fix-all)

+;;;###autoload
+(defun refactor-rename (newname backend)
+  "Rename the symbol at point to NEWNAME via BACKEND.
+Interactively, BACKEND is chosen to be the first backend in
+`refactor-backend-functions' that claims the symbol at point."
+  (interactive
+   (pcase-let ((`(,backend . ,bounds)
+                (cl-loop for b in (refactor-find-backends)
+                         when (refactor-backend-rename-bounds b)
+                         return (cons b it))))
+     (unless backend
+       (user-error "No backend can rename the symbol at point"))
+     (let ((sym-name (buffer-substring-no-properties (car bounds) (cdr bou=
nds))))
+       (list
+        (read-from-minibuffer (format "Rename `%s' to: " sym-name)
+         nil nil nil nil sym-name)
+        backend))))
+  (refactor-apply-changeset (refactor-backend-rename backend newname)
+                            :origin this-command))

+
+;;;; Suggestions
+
+;; Like in eglot, the state is a single overlay marking the bounds of
+;; the actions available at point; `refactor-suggestion' is an ElDoc
+;; member computing them, possibly asynchronously.
+;; `refactor-suggestion-mode' adds it to `eldoc-documentation-functions'
+;; and cleans up the overlay when disabled.  The mode's lighter is
+;; `refactor-mode-line-indicator', which shows `refactor-indicator'
+;; while the overlay exists.  Eglot, for one, does it when entering
+;; `eglot--managed-mode'.
+
+(defcustom refactor-indications '(eldoc-hint left-fringe margin)
+  "How refactor backends indicate there are actions available at point.
+Value is a list of symbols, more than one can be specified:
+
+- `eldoc-hint': ElDoc is used to hint about at-point actions;
+- `left-fringe': A special indicator appears on the left fringe;
+- `margin': A special indicator appears in the margin;
+- `nearby': A special indicator appears near point.
+
+If the list is empty, no hinting happens.
+
+Note additionally:
+
+- Some values are incompatible; if one or more of `nearby',
+  `left-fringe' and `margin' are specified, earlier values take
+  precedence.
+- The indicators for many of these are customizable via
+  `refactor-indicator' (which see), except for `left-fringe'."
+  :type '(set
+          :tag "Tick the ones you're interested in"
+          (const :tag "ElDoc textual hint" eldoc-hint)
+          (const :tag "Right besides point" nearby)
+          (const :tag "In left fringe" left-fringe)
+          (const :tag "In margin" margin)))
+
+(defface refactor-indicator-face
+  '((t (:inherit warning :weight bold)))
+  "Face used for action suggestions.")
+
+(defcustom refactor-indicator
+  (cl-loop for c in '(?=E2=86=AF ?=E2=AD=8D ?=E2=9C=93 ?=CE=B1 ??)
+           when (char-displayable-p c)
+           return (make-string 1 c))
+  "Indicator string for action suggestions."
+  :type (let ((basic-choices
+               (cl-loop for c in '(?=E2=86=AF ?=E2=AD=8D ?=E2=9C=93 ?=CE=
=B1 ??)
+                        when (char-displayable-p c)
+                        collect `(const :tag ,(format "Use `%c'" c)
+                                        ,(make-string 1 c)))))
+          `(choice ,@basic-choices
+                   (string :tag "Specify your own"))))
+
+(defvar-local refactor--suggestion-overlay (make-overlay 0 0)
+  "Overlay for `refactor-suggestion'.")
+
+(define-fringe-bitmap 'refactor--fringe-action
+  [#b00000111
+   #b00001110
+   #b00011100
+   #b00111000
+   #b01111111
+   #b00001110
+   #b01011100
+   #b01111000
+   #b01110000
+   #b01111000]
+  nil nil 'center)

+(defmacro refactor--when-buffer-window (buf &rest body)
+  "Check BUF showing somewhere, then do BODY in it."
+  (declare (indent 1) (debug t))
+  (let ((b (gensym)))
+    `(let ((,b ,buf))
+       (when (get-buffer-window ,b)
+         (with-current-buffer ,b ,@body)))))
+
+(defvar refactor-mouse-map
+  (let ((map (make-sparse-keymap)))
+    (define-key map [mouse-2] #'refactor-at-mouse)
+    (define-key map [left-margin mouse-1] #'refactor-at-mouse)
+    map)
+  "Keymap active on action indicators and clickable diagnostics.")
+
+(defun refactor-suggestion (cb &rest _)
+  "A member of `eldoc-documentation-functions', for suggesting actions."
+  (when (and refactor-indications (refactor-find-backends))
+    (let ((buf (current-buffer))
+          (bounds (refactor--bounds))
+          (use-text-p (memq 'eldoc-hint refactor-indications))
+          indicator blurb)
+      (refactor--collect
+       (car bounds) (cadr bounds)
+       :trigger-kind 2
+       :callback
+       (lambda (actions)
+         (refactor--when-buffer-window
+          buf
+          (when (overlay-buffer refactor--suggestion-overlay)
+            (delete-overlay refactor--suggestion-overlay))
+          (when (cl-plusp (length actions))
+            (setq blurb
+                  (substitute-command-keys
+                   (format "\\[refactor]: %s"
+                           (oref (car actions) title))))
+            (when (cdr actions)
+              (setq blurb (concat blurb (format " (and %s more actions)"
+                                                (length (cdr actions))))))
+            (setq indicator
+                  (propertize refactor-indicator
+                              'face 'refactor-indicator-face
+                              'help-echo "mouse-1: execute actions at poin=
t"
+                              'mouse-face 'highlight
+                              'keymap refactor-mouse-map))
+            (save-excursion
+              (goto-char (car bounds))
+              (let ((ov (make-overlay (car bounds) (cadr bounds))))
+                (overlay-put ov 'refactor--actions actions)
+                (overlay-put
+                 ov 'before-string
+                 (cond
+                  ((memq 'nearby refactor-indications)
+                   indicator)
+                  ((and (memq 'left-fringe refactor-indications)
+                        (< 0 (nth 0 (window-fringes))))
+                   (propertize
+                    "=E2=9A=A1" 'display `(left-fringe
+                                    refactor--fringe-action
+                                    refactor-indicator-face)))
+                  ((memq 'margin refactor-indications)
+                   (propertize
+                    "=E2=9A=A1" 'display `((margin left-margin) ,indicator=
)))))
+                (setq refactor--suggestion-overlay ov)))))
+         ;; Answer the ElDoc strategy even if BUF isn't showing, else it
+         ;; could wait for us forever (like in non-interactive tests).
+         (when use-text-p (funcall cb blurb))))
+      (and use-text-p t))))
+
+;;;###autoload
+(define-minor-mode refactor-suggestion-mode
+  "Minor mode for showing refactoring suggestions at point.
+Add `refactor-suggestion' to `eldoc-documentation-functions' and
+show `refactor-mode-line-indicator' while actions are available."
+  :init-value nil
+  :lighter refactor-mode-line-indicator
+  (if refactor-suggestion-mode
+      (add-hook 'eldoc-documentation-functions #'refactor-suggestion nil t)
+    (remove-hook 'eldoc-documentation-functions #'refactor-suggestion t)
+    (when (overlay-buffer refactor--suggestion-overlay)
+      (delete-overlay refactor--suggestion-overlay))))
+
+(defvar refactor--mode-line-map
+  (let ((map (make-sparse-keymap)))
+    (define-key map [mode-line mouse-1]
+                (refactor--mouse-call 'refactor-at-mouse t))
+    map)
+  "Keymap active on `refactor-mode-line-indicator'.")
+
+(defconst refactor-mode-line-indicator
+  '(:eval
+    (when (overlay-buffer refactor--suggestion-overlay)
+      `(" " (:propertize
+             ,refactor-indicator
+             face refactor-indicator-face
+             keymap ,refactor--mode-line-map
+             help-echo "mouse-1: execute actions at point"
+             mouse-face mode-line-highlight))))
+  "Mode line construct for at-point refactoring actions.")
+(put 'refactor-mode-line-indicator 'risky-local-variable t)

+
+;;;; Flymake integration
+
+;; Flymake backends may use these categories if they want their
+;; diagnostics to be clickable.  `refactor-mouse-map' contains
+;; a binding for `refactor-at-mouse'.
+(cl-loop
+ for i from 1
+ for type in '(refactor-note refactor-warning refactor-error)
+ for ftype in '(flymake-note flymake-warning flymake-error)
+ do
+ (put type 'flymake-category ftype)
+ (put type 'flymake-overlay-control
+      `((mouse-face . highlight)
+        (priority . ,(+ 50 i))
+        (keymap . ,refactor-mouse-map))))

+
+;;;; Applying changes
+
+(cl-defun refactor-apply-text-edits (edits &key silent)
+  "Apply EDITS to current buffer as single undoable step.
+
+EDITS is a list of (BEG END NEWTEXT), or a function of no
+arguments returning such a list, which is called with this buffer
+current.  BEG and END are positions valid in the widened buffer.
+Edits must not overlap, but need not be sorted.
+
+Unless SILENT, report progress in the echo area."
+  (when (functionp edits) (setq edits (funcall edits)))
+  (unless edits (cl-return-from refactor-apply-text-edits))
+  (atomic-change-group
+    (let* ((change-group (prepare-change-group))
+           (howmany (length edits))
+           (reporter (unless silent
+                       (make-progress-reporter
+                        (format "Applying %s edits to `%s'..."
+                                howmany (current-buffer))
+                        0 howmany)))
+           (done 0))
+      ;; Convert every edit to markers up front, so that applying one
+      ;; cannot invalidate the positions of the others.
+      (mapc (pcase-lambda (`(,beg ,end ,newtext))
+              (if (> emacs-major-version 30)
+                  (replace-region-contents beg end newtext)
+                ;; Before Emacs 31, `replace-region-contents' wanted a
+                ;; function, so go through a temporary buffer.
+                (let ((source (current-buffer)))
+                  (with-temp-buffer
+                    (insert newtext)
+                    (let ((temp (current-buffer)))
+                      (with-current-buffer source
+                        (save-excursion
+                          (save-restriction
+                            (narrow-to-region beg end)
+                            (with-no-warnings
+                              (replace-buffer-contents temp)))))))))
+              (when reporter
+                (progress-reporter-update reporter (cl-incf done))))
+            (mapcar (pcase-lambda (`(,beg ,end ,newtext))
+                      (list (copy-marker beg) (copy-marker end) newtext))
+                    (reverse edits)))
+      (undo-amalgamate-change-group change-group)
+      (when reporter (progress-reporter-done reporter)))))
+
+(defcustom refactor-confirmation '((t . maybe-summary))
+  "Control if changes proposed by a backend should be confirmed with user.
+
+If this variable's value is the symbol `diff', a diff buffer pops
+up, allowing the user to apply each change individually.  If the
+symbol `summary' or any other non-nil value, the user is prompted
+in the minibuffer with a short summary of changes.  The symbols
+`maybe-diff' and `maybe-summary' mean that the confirmation is
+offered to the user only if the changes target files not visited
+in buffers.  Finally, a nil value means all changes are applied
+directly without any confirmation.
+
+This variable's value can also be an alist ((KEY . ACTION) ...)
+where KEY is either a symbol designating the invoked Emacs command
+\(such as `refactor-rename', `refactor', `refactor-quickfix',
+etc.), or a list of file operation kinds (`create', `rename',
+`delete') contained in the changeset.  ACTION is one of the
+symbols described above.  The value t for KEY is accepted and its
+ACTION is the default value for commands or file operation kinds
+not in the alist."
+  :type (let ((basic-choices
+               '((const :tag "Use diff" diff)
+                 (const :tag "Summarize and prompt" summary)
+                 (const :tag "Maybe use diff" maybe-diff)
+                 (const :tag "Maybe summarize and prompt" maybe-summary)
+                 (const :tag "Don't confirm" nil))))
+          `(choice ,@basic-choices
+                   (alist :tag "Per-command or per-kind alist"
+                          :key-type (choice (function :tag "Command")
+                                            (repeat :tag "File operation k=
inds" symbol)
+                                            (const :tag "Default" t))
+                          :value-type (choice . ,basic-choices))))
+  :version "32.1")
+
+(defconst refactor--changes-buffer-name "*refactor changes*"
+  "Name of the buffer used to preview proposed changes as a diff.")
+
+(defun refactor--confirmation (origin operations)
+  "Return the confirmation ACTION to use for OPERATIONS.
+ORIGIN is a symbol designating the command that asked for them.  Reads
+`refactor-confirmation' and returns a symbol like `diff' or `summary',
+or nil to apply without confirming."
+  (let ((v (lambda (candidate) (cdr (assq candidate refactor-confirmation)=
)))
+        kinds)
+    (or (and (symbolp refactor-confirmation) refactor-confirmation)
+        ;; Check for command-based entry
+        (funcall v origin)
+        ;; Check for operation-kind-based entry
+        (and (setq kinds (mapcar #'refactor-operation-kind operations))
+             (cl-some (lambda (entry)
+                        (and (listp (car entry))
+                             (cl-some (lambda (kind)
+                                        (memq kind (car entry)))
+                                      kinds)
+                             (cdr entry)))
+                      refactor-confirmation))
+        ;; Default entry
+        (funcall v t))))
+
+(cl-defgeneric refactor--apply-operation (operation)
+  "Carry OPERATION out."
+  (:method ((op refactor-file-edit))
+   (with-slots (file edits) op
+     (with-current-buffer (find-file-noselect file)
+       (refactor-apply-text-edits edits))))
+  (:method ((op refactor-file-creation))
+   (with-slots (file contents if-exists) op
+     (let ((exists (file-exists-p file)))
+       (when (and exists (eq if-exists 'error))
+         (error "File %s already exists" file))
+       (when (or (not exists) (eq if-exists 'overwrite))
+         (let ((dir (file-name-directory file)))
+           (unless (file-directory-p dir) (make-directory dir t)))
+         (write-region (or contents "") nil file nil 'nomessage)))))
+  (:method ((op refactor-file-renaming))
+   (with-slots (from to if-exists) op
+     (let ((new-exists (file-exists-p to)))
+       (when (and new-exists (eq if-exists 'error))
+         (error "File %s already exists" to))
+       (unless (and new-exists (eq if-exists 'skip))
+         (let ((dir (file-name-directory to)))
+           (unless (file-directory-p dir) (make-directory dir t)))
+         ;; If the old file is visited, rename the buffer too
+         (when-let* ((buf (find-buffer-visiting from)))
+           (with-current-buffer buf (set-visited-file-name to t t)))
+         (rename-file from to (eq if-exists 'overwrite))))))
+  (:method ((op refactor-file-deletion))
+   (with-slots (file recursive if-missing) op
+     (let ((exists (file-exists-p file)))
+       (when (and (not exists) (eq if-missing 'error))
+         (error "File %s does not exist" file))
+       (when exists
+         ;; Kill the buffer if the file is visited
+         (when-let* ((buf (find-buffer-visiting file))) (kill-buffer buf))
+         (delete-file file recursive))))))
+
+(defun refactor--apply-and-report (operation)
+  "Carry OPERATION out and say so in the echo area."
+  (refactor--apply-operation operation)
+  (unless (refactor-file-edit-p operation)
+    (message "%s" (replace-regexp-in-string
+                   "^\\([^ ]+\\) " "\\1d "
+                   (refactor-describe operation)))))
+
+(defun refactor--file-text (file)
+  "Insert the full text of FILE into the current buffer.
+If a buffer is visiting FILE, take the text from there instead,
+disregarding any narrowing, so that positions in the result agree
+with positions in the widened buffer."
+  (if-let* ((buf (find-buffer-visiting file)))
+      (insert (with-current-buffer buf
+                (save-restriction
+                  (widen)
+                  (buffer-substring-no-properties (point-min) (point-max))=
)))
+    (insert-file-contents file)))
+
+(defun refactor--propose-changes-as-diff (operations)
+  "Return a `diff-mode' buffer with the changes OPERATIONS would make.
+OPERATIONS are all `refactor-file-edit's.  The buffer is ready to
+apply with \\<diff-mode-map>\\[diff-apply-buffer]."
+  (with-current-buffer (get-buffer-create refactor--changes-buffer-name)
+    (buffer-disable-undo (current-buffer))
+    (let ((inhibit-read-only t)
+          (target (current-buffer)))
+      (diff-mode)
+      (erase-buffer)
+      (dolist (op operations)
+        (with-temp-buffer
+          (let* ((diff (current-buffer))
+                 (path (oref op file))
+                 (existing-buf (find-buffer-visiting path))
+                 (existing-buf-label (prin1-to-string existing-buf)))
+            (with-temp-buffer
+              (refactor--file-text path)
+              (refactor-apply-text-edits (oref op edits)
+                                         :silent t)
+              (diff-no-select (or existing-buf path) (current-buffer) nil =
t diff)
+              (when existing-buf
+                ;; Here we have to pretend the label of the unsaved
+                ;; buffer is the actual file, so that `diff-apply-buffer'
+                ;; works.  If there's a better way, it probably involves
+                ;; changes to `diff.el'.
+                (with-current-buffer diff
+                  (goto-char (point-min))
+                  (while (search-forward existing-buf-label nil t)
+                    (replace-match (buffer-file-name existing-buf))))))
+            (with-current-buffer target
+              (insert-buffer-substring diff))))))
+    (setq-local buffer-read-only t)
+    (buffer-enable-undo (current-buffer))
+    (goto-char (point-min))
+    (font-lock-ensure)
+    (current-buffer)))
+
+(cl-defun refactor-apply-changeset (operations &key origin)
+  "Apply OPERATIONS, a changeset, after confirming with the user.
+
+OPERATIONS is a list of `refactor-operation' objects, applied in
+order.  ORIGIN is a symbol designating the command that produced
+them; `refactor-confirmation' may key on it.
+
+Return a list (APPLIED REASON) saying whether the changes were
+applied and, if not, why not; REASON is nil when they were."
+  (cl-labels
+      ((user-accepts-p ()
+         (y-or-n-p
+          (format "These changes will be made:\n%s\nProceed? "
+                  (mapconcat (lambda (op)
+                               (concat "  " (refactor-describe op)))
+                             operations "\n"))))
+       (apply-all ()
+         (mapc #'refactor--apply-and-report operations)
+         (eldoc)
+         (message "Refactoring applied")
+         `(t nil)))
+    (let* ((decision (refactor--confirmation origin operations))
+           (all-edits (cl-every #'refactor-file-edit-p operations))
+           (peaceful (and all-edits
+                          (cl-every (lambda (op)
+                                      (find-buffer-visiting (oref op file)=
))
+                                    operations))))
+      (cond
+       ((and (memq decision '(maybe-diff maybe-summary)) peaceful)
+        (apply-all))
+       ((memq decision '(diff maybe-diff))
+        (cond (all-edits
+               (pop-to-buffer (refactor--propose-changes-as-diff operation=
s))
+               `(nil "decision to apply manually"))
+              (t
+               ;; `map-y-or-n-p' heroics.  Iterate over operations with
+               ;; individual prompts, showing diffs for edits.
+               (let* ((wconf (current-window-configuration))
+                      (remaining operations)
+                      (applied 0)
+                      (total (length operations)))
+                 (unwind-protect
+                     (progn
+                       (map-y-or-n-p
+                        (lambda (op)
+                          (when (refactor-file-edit-p op)
+                            (display-buffer
+                             (refactor--propose-changes-as-diff (list op))=
))
+                          (format "%s? " (refactor-describe op)))
+                        (lambda (op)
+                          (set-window-configuration wconf)
+                          (refactor--apply-and-report op)
+                          (cl-incf applied))
+                        (lambda ()
+                          ;; Skip edits to files that don't exist (e.g.
+                          ;; the user skipped the create operation).
+                          (cl-loop for op =3D (pop remaining) while op
+                                   when (or (not (refactor-file-edit-p op))
+                                            (file-exists-p (oref op file)))
+                                   return op))
+                        '("change" "changes" "apply"))
+                       (if (=3D applied total)
+                           (progn
+                             (eldoc)
+                             (message "Refactoring applied")
+                             `(t nil))
+                         `(nil "decision to abort")))
+                   (set-window-configuration wconf))))))
+       ((memq decision '(t summary maybe-summary))
+        (if (user-accepts-p) (apply-all) `(nil "decision to decline")))
+       ((apply-all))))))
+
+(provide 'refactor)
+;;; refactor.el ends here
